In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: What are the best Boolean satisfiability modeling techniques for circuit delay computation, taking into account the presence of false paths? What are the best algorithms for solving such instances? How complex are real-world instances of circuit delay computation?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the best algorithms for solving circuit delay problems are the ones based on the DPLL procedure, with conflict-directed backtracking, and the ones using the Davis-Putnam procedure, with conflict-clause learning and unit propagation.
the best algorithm for solving delay computation problems is MiniSat, followed by Chaff and Berkmin.
solving circuit delay computation as a sequence of SAT problems is an efficient approach for the majority of the instances studied, but it is not the most appropriate one for all of them.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the problem is NP-hard, that it can be solved by a combination of Boolean satisfiability algorithms, and that it is not a problem of the same complexity as the satisfiability problem.

, in spite of the fact that solving circuit delay problems is a computationally hard task, the use of state-of-the-art Boolean satisfiability algorithms is able to solve a significant number of instances in an efficient manner, even for realistic delay modeling.

the best algorithms for delay computation, when considering realistic delay models and real circuits, are based on a combination of Boolean constraint propagation and Boolean satisfiability algorithms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a given delay model and path sensitization model, the complexity of solving circuit delay computation instances as Boolean satisfiability instances is highly dependent on the algorithm used.
, despite being NP-hard problems, circuit delay computation instances can be solved in reasonable time by using the state-of-the-art Boolean satisfiability algorithms.
, despite the fact that the delay computation problems are NP-hard, they can be effectively solved in practice using state-of-the-art Boolean satisfiability solvers.
